answer: The dome is turned by hand for every show, and the rotation record logs its position at the start and end of each evening. A thread dome worked by a hired hand fails the record: at the mirror of the turn the position must match the evening's own entry, and a hired hand turns it to the wrong star. Faking the record means running the planetarium for a season, logging 110 shows and paying 13,200, and the onyx figure in the record book is checked before every performance, so a show that was never given is struck from the list.
